text:
Nashville has gone on a winning run, and Nick Perbix has been part of the furniture through it, playing roughly 18 to 21 minutes a night. He's chipped in too: his first goal of the season against Carolina on Nov 3, then an empty-netter against St. Louis four nights later, for 4 points in 19 games.

He's a positional defender, not a physical one: 33 blocked shots and just 4 hits. The underlying numbers urge some caution about how much of the winning runs through him. At five on five Nashville has had 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Perbix on the ice, about 4 points worse than without him, and last season Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level (-0.5 wins). His scoring is roughly where his chances say it should be, and our range has him finishing with 11 to 23 points. A sixth-round pick by Tampa Bay in 2017 who played for the U.S. at the 2022 Olympics, he has carved out a steady job on the right side. What we'd watch is whether his pair can keep chances down once the bounces even out.
headline: Perbix is on the ice for Nashville's winning run
